analysis.title: Cognizant Technology Solutions (CTSH): Solid margin performance, but guidance downtick on weaker discretionary trends
key_insights: GS expects CTSH to trade down modestly after a 3Q26 print with a guidance downtick. Weaker discretionary spending in Healthcare (Health Sciences) and Consumer drove the cut.

Investor sentiment had improved on solid results from peers Accenture and IBM but remains cautious on macro. Softer 4Q guidance and weaker bookings in the quarter likely reinforce skepticism about a fundamental acceleration.
Financial Services sustained double-digit revenue growth. Management sees the vertical as a leading indicator for broader demand recovery.
Sequential gross margin stabilized even as large deals ramp. Management says higher AI-led productivity gains offset pricing pressure.
Management said overall discretionary demand has downticked on macro headwinds. Uncertainty is elevated in Health Sciences and Products & Resources because of policy and geopolitical risks.
4Q26 revenue view is more cautious: about 200bps organic and about 200bps inorganic growth expected.
FY26 operating margin guidance is maintained. Project Leap adds 20-40bps of expansion, with savings of about $200mn in 2026. The program now extends into 1Q27.
Management still expects gross and operating margin expansion in 2027.
Cognizant reported over 8,500 AI engagements in the quarter, versus 8,000 in 1Q26. AI now assists over 50% of software development.
Cognizant sees agentic BPO as a medium-term growth driver, potentially widening the addressable market from roughly $1tn in systems integration to a $5-6tn enterprise-operations opportunity.
3Q26 revenue of $5.66bn, EPS of $1.49 and non-GAAP gross margin of 33.8% were all above the Street. Free cash flow of $925mn was below the Street at $948mn, and 3Q26 bookings fell 7% Y/Y.
FY26 constant-currency revenue growth guidance was cut to 4.0%-4.4%, below GS at 4.7% and the Street at 4.6%.
4Q26 constant-currency growth guidance of 3.2%-4.7% is below GS at 6.3% and the Street at 5.9%.
GS cut 2027/2028 EPS estimates to $6.25/$6.70 from $6.35/$6.85, mainly on lower revenue. 2026 EPS moved up slightly to $5.78 from $5.75.

GS maintains Neutral with a $70 12-month price target (11x one-year forward EPS). It would be more constructive on evidence that Cognizant captures rising AI demand and the discretionary recovery while gross margin keeps improving.
GS views the results as a modest incremental negative for its IT Services coverage.

market_movers.rationale: Neutral maintained with a $70 target, 11x one-year forward EPS. GS sees Cognizant in the early to middle stages of its pivot to stronger growth. The 2026 revenue guide was cut on weaker discretionary demand.

sector_views.rationale: GS calls the CTSH results a modest incremental negative for its IT Services coverage because of the 2026 guidance downtick.

earnings_insights: CTSH 3Q26 reported revenue $5.66bn (GS est $5.64bn, Street est per Visible Alpha), up 4.6% Y/Y as reported and 4.8% in constant currency.
CTSH 3Q26 non-GAAP EPS from continuing operations reported $1.49 vs Street est $1.46 and GS est $1.44, up 7.5% Y/Y.
CTSH 3Q26 reported non-GAAP gross margin 33.8% vs Street est 33.6% and GS est 33.4%. Non-GAAP operating margin was 16.3%.
CTSH 3Q26 reported adjusted free cash flow $925mn vs Street est $948mn, against $1,160mn in 3Q25.
CTSH FY26 guidance: constant-currency revenue growth 4.0%-4.4% (GS est 4.7%, Street est 4.6%), revenue $22.05-22.14bn (midpoint below Street est $22.19bn and GS est $22.2bn).
CTSH FY26 guidance: adjusted operating margin 16.1% (GS est 16.1%, Street est 16.0%). Adjusted EPS guidance narrowed to $5.72-$5.79 (GS est $5.75, Street est $5.76).
CTSH 4Q26 guidance: constant-currency growth 3.2%-4.7% (GS est 6.3%, Street est 5.9%), revenue $5.49-$5.57bn (GS est $5.66bn, Street est $5.65bn).
GS revised non-GAAP EPS estimates to $5.78 (2026), $6.25 (2027) and $6.70 (2028), from $5.75, $6.35 and $6.85.

vol_and_positioning: Investor sentiment on CTSH had somewhat improved after Accenture and IBM results but remains cautious. GS expects the stock to trade down modestly after the print.

tension_points.bull_case: Financial Services sustained double-digit growth and is seen by management as a leading indicator of broader demand recovery. Gross margin stabilized as AI productivity offsets pricing pressure, and AI engagements rose to 8,500.
tension_points.bear_case: Discretionary demand downticked in Healthcare and Consumer, bookings fell 7% Y/Y and 4Q guidance is below the Street, which reinforces skepticism about a fundamental acceleration.
tension_points.what_invalidates: GS could turn more constructive if Cognizant shows it is fully participating in the discretionary demand recovery while gross margin keeps improving.
